idea_title: Account-free daily microgames with a deliberate no-monetization stance
snippet: Rising since Nov 3 2026: lightweight casual games that run instantly in browsers with no downloads, no accounts and no ads, built around daily habits and social sharing. 23 signals this week from 4 sources, momentum 35/100.
why_hot: 23 signals in one week, momentum 35/100, rising since 2026-11-03: the frictionless no-account microgame format is being tracked as its own trend, not a niche.
core_mechanic: A one-screen daily microgame that opens straight into play, keeps a local streak, and shares a spoiler-free result link with zero signup.
audience: Commuter and coffee-break players on phones, 2 to 5 minute sessions
monetization: None in-product; brand surface for the catalog

idea_title: Tiny planet you can circumnavigate in minutes
snippet: Messenger is a free browser exploration game where players deliver letters across a tiny stylized planet whose curvature is visible a few steps ahead. Went viral on 2026-06-15 after a single tweet, 5.7 MB initial load, multiplayer presence limited to emoji.
why_hot: Viral in June 2026 from one tweet: the hook is a world small enough to walk all the way around in minutes, and the multiplayer layer is presence only, no chat and no competition.
core_mechanic: A bounded curved world with no map screen: progress is spatial and memorable because the whole world fits in the player's head.
audience: Exploration and cozy-game players, desktop and mobile browser
monetization: Premium game sold on web, no ads

snippet: Claude Kart: a Mario Kart-inspired 3D browser racing game, three.js r174 plus WebGPU and TSL, procedural track, drift mechanics and power-ups, entire game in one index.html of about 800 lines with zero build step. Claims WebGPU is baseline across major browsers in 2026.
why_hot: WebGPU became baseline in 2026 and this shows the ceiling of one-file browser games: 800 lines, no build, procedural audio, playable instantly.
core_mechanic: Drift-and-boost kart racing against AI on a procedural circuit, with power-up pickups and a single-file zero-dependency build.
audience: Arcade racing fans on desktop browsers with gamepad or keyboard

idea_title: One-button bank-or-crash game with a score brag link
snippet: A one-button vanilla JS canvas game: hold to bank, risk a crash, screen shake and particle feedback. The viral hook is one URL parameter, ?s=<score>, so whoever opens a shared link sees 'a friend banked $4,200, beat them' with no backend and no accounts.
why_hot: The whole social layer is a score in a URL: no backend, no accounts, and the challenge line is generated from the link. Zero-friction virality in about 2k lines of single-file JS.
core_mechanic: Press-and-hold risk timing: the longer you hold the higher the multiplier and the closer the crash, with one decision per run.
audience: Casual arcade players on phones, 30 second sessions

idea_title: Poki's review bar: retention first, no death in the first three minutes
snippet: Poki reviews every submitted game. Retention is the single most important metric; the first three minutes decide it, and players should not be able to die in that window. File size is a dealbreaker and touch controls matter. A game built around one mechanic executed well is a legitimate web game.
why_hot: A portal that reviews every submission states the actual bar in numbers: retention first, no failure in the first three minutes, small files, touch-first. That is a testable acceptance list.
core_mechanic: Difficulty curve shaped so the first three minutes are unloseable, then ramps once the player has committed.
audience: Portal-scale casual web players, mostly mobile browsers

idea_title: Prestige loop as the retention engine for browser incrementals
snippet: Research synthesis on browser game addiction and viral mechanics: compulsion loops, prestige as the single most important retention mechanic in incremental games, and three original single-file concepts under 50KB with localStorage saves and no dependencies.
why_hot: Names prestige as the strongest retention mechanic in the incremental genre and pairs it with a single-file, under-50KB, no-dependency constraint that matches this repo's shipping model.
core_mechanic: Reset-for-permanent-multiplier progression: the player voluntarily restarts with a compounding bonus, so every session makes the next one faster.
audience: Idle and incremental players, long-tail desktop sessions
